highlights.title: SpaceX’s Musk, David Sacks to Join Altman, Huang at G20 Event
highlights.description: SpaceX Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk, who ran a brazen campaign in Washington to cut government spending last year, and former White House AI czar David Sacks are scheduled to speak at a tech-focused Group of 20 ministerial meeting in North Carolina next week, along with Nvidia Corp.’s Jensen Huang and OpenAI’s Sam Altman, people familiar with the matter said.

highlights.title: OpenAI, Anthropic Urge Cyber Defense Action as AI Models Improve
highlights.description: Artificial intelligence companies OpenAI and Anthropic PBC, along with more than 100 other tech and financial services organizations, warned that businesses and governments must do more to prepare for and defend against AI-enabled hacks.

highlights.title: OpenAI to End Partnership With Cursor After SpaceX Acquisition
highlights.description: OpenAI said it will end its partnership with Cursor after the AI-coding agent’s acquisition by SpaceX, according to a post on X.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang says Nvidia achieved AGI, again — not that it matters
highlights.description: On Nvidia's earnings call Wednesday, CEO Jensen Huang casually announced the company had "achieved AGI," one of the tech industry's ultimate goals some of its biggest players have spent years chasing. Almost immediately, Huang dismissed the coveted milestone as "senseless." He's right. For the supposed finish line of the AI race, there is no consensus on what artificial general intelligence means, let alone how we'll know when we've actually got there, which makes achieving it equally arbitrary.

highlights.title: Nvidia closes in on Hugging Face acquisition

robotics.title: Hugging Face Unveils $400 Singing, Skating Duck-Like Robot
robotics.description: Artificial intelligence platform Hugging Face Inc. unveiled a singing $400 bipedal robot that can be taught tricks, the latest in the company’s ongoing effort to make AI and robotics more approachable to the general public.The cute robot — aptly named Microduck — takes clear inspiration from its namesake bird, except that it has only one eye. It will go on sale later this year, Hugging Face said Thursday, making it the second robot from the company.
